BO.name: Ayahuasca
BO.citation: Traditional use documented across the Amazon basin extending from southern Bolivia to northern Panama (NTBG Tropical Plants Database); no distinct Bolivia-specific name found beyond the shared Quechua-derived regional term

BR.name: Mariri
BR.citation: Peer-reviewed mitogenomic study (PMC11234496, Universidade Estadual Paulista/UFRJ/UFABC), documenting 'Mariri or Jagube' as the Brazilian name used by Indigenous communities and syncretic religious groups (Santo Daime, Uniao do Vegetal). Also documented as 'hoasca' in Brazil (PMC6646606)

CO.name: Yaje
CO.citation: PMC6646606 (peer-reviewed phytochemical review), explicitly noting 'In Colombia it is also called caapi or yaje'; documented use by Shaman communities in Putumayo, Colombia

EC.name: Natema
EC.citation: PMC6646606 (peer-reviewed phytochemical review), documenting 'Nate' as the Ecuador-specific name. The oldest known ayahuasca-related ceremonial artifact (a cup dated to 50 AD) was found in Ecuador

PE.name: Ayahuasca
PE.citation: ICEERS; Quechua term composed of 'aya' (corpse/spirit) and 'waskha' (rope/vine). Used in the Peruvian Amazon for millennia, predating the Inca Empire. Note: this entry names the vine itself; 'ayahuasca' also separately denotes the brewed decoction made from it

US.name: Ayahuasca
US.citation: UC Berkeley BCSP; genuine legal/religious recognition exists in the US for ayahuasca ceremonies conducted by the Santo Daime and Uniao do Vegetal (UDV) religious movements

VE.name: Ayahuasca
VE.citation: Traditional healing use documented among Orinoco basin native healers (PMC6646606); no distinct Venezuela-specific vernacular name found beyond the shared regional term
